concerns.text: Tasks T018a, T019, and T025a explicitly implement a 'SINGLE' Greedy Maximal Dissimilarity Split and perform the Corrected Resampled t-test on 'single held-out test set predictions'. This violates Constitution Principle VII (FR-030) which mandates '5-fold cross-validation scores' and the Spec's FR-005 which requires the t-test to be valid. The Corrected Resampled t-test (Nadeau & Bengio) is mathematically invalid on a single split; the tasks silently weaken the statistical rigor required by the Constitution and Spec.

Task T018a implements a 'SINGLE' split, whereas the Plan (which aligns with Constitution VII) explicitly requires 'K-Fold Cross-Validation' with a Greedy Split per fold. The tasks drop the K-Fold requirement entirely, violating the methodological constraint established in the Plan and Constitution to ensure statistical validity.

Tasks T013a and T013b are marked as 'FAILED: unspecified' or depend on failed logic. The Spec's 'Data Scarcity' edge case mandates a specific handling path (warning + skip stats) for n < 50. The current task list fails to define a working implementation for this critical acceptance criterion, effectively dropping the requirement to handle low sample sizes gracefully.

Task T025c3 compares raw Gini importance sums between Morgan (2048 bits) and MACCS (166 bits) without normalization. The Spec's SC-003 requires measuring if Morgan bits are 'more predictive' by a 15% margin. Comparing raw sums of vectors with vastly different dimensions (2048 vs 166) without normalization violates the semantic intent of the success criterion, as the larger vector size inherently inflates the sum, making the 15% threshold meaningless and the test untestable.
